subject: Architecture
title: The Surfside Condo Collapse in Miami
description: A quick, practical guide to The Surfside Condo Collapse in Miami.

hook.text: At 1:22 AM on June 24, 2021, half of a 12-story condo in Miami collapsed while residents slept. 98 people died.

buildup.text: Champlain Towers South was built in 1981 on reclaimed wetland near the ocean — exposed to saltwater corrosion.

discovery.text: A 2018 engineering report warned of 'major structural damage' in the pool deck and garage. Repairs were delayed.

twist.text: Corroded rebar in the concrete had been expanding for years, cracking the structure from the inside out.

climax.text: Florida passed landmark laws requiring regular structural inspections for aging condo buildings.

punchline.text: The warning came three years early. The repairs came too late.

quiz.question: What caused the structural deterioration at Champlain Towers?
options: Earthquake damage weakened the foundation over decades
Corroded rebar expanded and cracked the concrete from within
Hurricane winds stripped the exterior cladding repeatedly

details.summary: Champlain Towers South in Surfside, Florida, partially collapsed on June 24, 2021, killing 98 people. A 2018 engineering report had warned of major structural damage to the pool deck and columns, but repairs were delayed by bureaucracy and cost disputes among condo owners.
details.whyItMatters: Surfside revealed that America's aging concrete buildings face maintenance crises that bureaucratic structures are poorly equipped to handle. It triggered nationwide inspections and new legislation requiring periodic structural recertification.
takeaways: Champlain Towers South collapsed in 2021, killing 98 people
A 2018 report warned of major structural damage but repairs stalled
It triggered nationwide building inspection and recertification reform

faq.question: What caused the Surfside condo collapse?
faq.answer: Decades of water infiltration corroded the reinforcing steel in the pool deck and ground-floor columns. The waterproofing was improperly installed flat rather than sloped, allowing standing water.

faq.question: Could the collapse have been prevented?
faq.answer: Yes. The 2018 engineering report identified the exact problems that caused the collapse. Repairs estimated at $9-15 million were debated by the condo association for three years. By the time repairs were approved, the deterioration had progressed past the point of no return.
